subject: P95 latency spike: stabilization playbook and customer updates
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@amplifyai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: P95 latency spike: initial notice and immediate mitigations

Hi Alex,

Wanted to reach out directly — our telemetry started showing a sustained p95 latency increase for text-generation requests routing through our us-west GPU pool beginning ~08:30 PDT. Initial triage indicates a combination of KV-cache churn on a subset of hosts and an unexpected sequence-length distribution spike from a small customer cohort.

Impact we’re seeing: 5–10% of requests in that pool have p95 elevations in the 2.5–3s range (typical p95 is ~600–800ms for your workload). We are treating this as elevated and have the on-call infra and serving teams actively working on containment.

Immediate actions we have taken: 
- Isolated the affected GPU shards and enabled routing fallback to our warm standby pool.
- Triggered reduced prefetching on candidates that cause large KV churn.
- Deployed a temporary small-scale rate limiting advisory for noisy model variants.

Attached a short ops playbook (ops_playbook_v1.pdf) with the knobs we plan to run while we stabilize. We will post a public incident entry to our status page and follow up with a technical update in 60–90 minutes.

How you’ll be impacted: we expect most API calls to continue to succeed; some p95 responses may be higher during the mitigation window. If Amplify prefers, we can pin your traffic to a dedicated warm pool for the next 24 hours to prevent variability — that would require a short config change from our side.

Please let me know if you want us to enable the pinning immediately. We’ll keep you updated in-line here and via status.redwoodinference.com.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@amplifyai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amplify AI Ops <ops@amplifyai.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: P95 latency spike: initial notice and immediate mitigations

Jonas — thanks for the quick heads up.

We started seeing timeouts in our customer chat autosuggest flow around 09:00 PDT. A few notes from our side:
- Chat autosuggest uses short-context sessions but high QPS (spiky bursts), so p95 matters a lot for user-perceived latency.
- We’re not on a dedicated pool today. Pinning to a warm pool for 24 hours sounds like it would help; please proceed if it’s low friction.

Can you confirm if there are any expected request-level retries we should disable client-side while you do the switch (to avoid duplication)? Also appreciate the ETA for the next update.

— Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Integrations | Amplify AI
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@amplifyai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: P95 latency spike: initial notice and immediate mitigations

Alex — thanks, confirmed we’ll flip Amplify to the dedicated warm pool now.

Operational notes for Amplify:
- We will perform a seamless routing change that should not require client-side retry changes. We recommend keeping your current client retry strategy (short 250ms backoff) during the 5–10 minute window; we will suppress duplicate delivery where possible.
- If you have very latency-sensitive endpoints, you can also enable a short client-side 3xx fallback to your cached suggestions while we complete stabilization.

Technical summary of what we’re doing:
1) Warm-pool pin: routing rule applied at the edge -> expected reduction in observed p95 within 90s.
2) KV eviction tuning on implicated hosts: reduces cache churn and improves next-token latency by lowering overhead for large sequences.
3) Temporary model-variant dampening: noisy variants will be deprioritized for 30–60m while we validate stability.

We’ve attached the p95 metrics slice for your traffic and the global view (p95_metrics_20260823.csv). We’ll continue to monitor and post another update once the warm-pool pin completes and we confirm p95 improvement.

Laura Bennett
Senior Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: p95_metrics_20260823.csv (csv stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@amplifyai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: stabilization complete and next steps

Alex — quick follow-up now that the incident window is closed. Summary and next steps: 

What happened: a confluence of heavy short-session bursts plus an unexpected model-variant pattern caused elevated KV-cache churn on a subset of us-west serving shards, which pushed p95 higher for a small percentage of traffic.

What we did: 
- Pinned Amplify traffic to a warm pool (completed 2026-08-23T10:08 PDT).
- Tuned eviction policy and throttled noisy variants.
- Rotated the affected serving hosts and validated KV-hit rates improved.

Outcome: p95 for Amplify traffic returned to baseline (~650ms) by 10:30 PDT on 2026-08-23. We kept the warm-pool pin for 24h and removed it at 2026-08-24T10:00 PDT after additional validation.

Action items we’ll deliver in the next 5 business days:
- Postmortem doc (link below) with timeline, root cause analysis, and permanent mitigations.
- New routing rule to avoid cross-tenant noisy-variant exposure under high short-session QPS.
- An optional client-side guidance note (short best-practices) for Amplify to further harden against transient retries.

External references:
- Incident entry: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/2026-08-23-usw-p95
- Postmortem draft (internal): https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/RI-5421

If you’d like a short 15-minute sync to walk through the postmortem once the draft is ready, I’m happy to schedule. Appreciate your patience and the quick collaboration from your ops team.

Regards,
Jonas
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
